'''Alessio Figalli''' ({{IPA|it|aˈlɛssjo fiˈɡalli|lang}}; born 2 April 1984) is an Italian [[mathematician]] working primarily on the [[calculus of variations]] and [[partial differential equation]]s.

He was awarded the Peccot-Vimont Prize and the [[Peccot Lectures]] in 2012, the [[EMS Prize]] in 2012,<ref>{{cite web|title=6th European Congress of Mathematics|url=http://www.6ecm.pl/docs/6ecm-prizes.pdf|publisher=European mathematical Society|accessdate=13 March 2013}}</ref> the [[Stampacchia Medal]] in 2015,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://umi.dm.unibo.it/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/motivazioni_figalli.pdf|title=2015 Stampacchia Medal winner citation|publisher=}}</ref> the [[Feltrinelli Prize]] in 2017, and the [[Fields Medal]] in 2018. He was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM 2014 |url=http://www.icm2014.org/en/program/scientific/topics |url-status = dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106014030/http://www.icm2014.org/en/program/scientific/topics |archivedate=6 November 2014 }}</ref>
In 2016 he was awarded a [[European Research Council]] (ERC) grant, and in 2018 he received the Doctorate ''Honoris Causa'' from the [[University of Côte d'Azur|Université Côte d'Azur]]. In 2019, he received the Doctorate ''Honoris Causa'' from the [[Polytechnic University of Catalonia]].

==Biography==
Figalli received his master's degree from the [[University of Pisa]]<ref>[https://etd.adm.unipi.it/theses/available/etd-06052006-100000/ SISTEMA ETD - Archivio digitale delle tesi discusse presso l'Università di Pisa]</ref> in 2006 (as a student of the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]]), and earned his doctorate in 2007 under the supervision of [[Luigi Ambrosio]] at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]] and [[Cédric Villani]] at the [[École Normale Supérieure de Lyon]]. In 2007, he was appointed Chargé de recherche at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]], and in 2008 he went to the [[École polytechnique]] as Professeur Hadamard.<ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=https://people.math.ethz.ch/~afigalli/cv-pdf/cv-pdf.pdf|title=Alessio Figalli – Curriculum vitae|access-date=2025-01-16}}</ref>

In 2009, he moved to the [[University of Texas at Austin]] as an associate professor. He became full professor in 2011, and [[Robert Lee Moore|R. L. Moore]] Chair holder in 2013. Since 2016, he is a chaired professor at [[ETH Zurich|ETH Zürich]].<ref name=cv/>

Amongst his several recognitions, Figalli has won an [[EMS Prize]] in 2012, he has been awarded the Peccot-Vimont Prize 2011 and Cours Peccot 2012 of the [[Collège de France]] and has been appointed Nachdiplom Lecturer in 2014 at [[ETH Zurich|ETH Zürich]].<ref>{{cite web|title=ETH Lectures in Mathematics|url=https://people.math.ethz.ch/~struwe/ND/nachdiplom.html}}</ref> He has won the 2015 edition of the [[Stampacchia Medal]], and the 2017 edition of the [[Feltrinelli Prize]] for mathematics.

In 2018, he won the [[Fields Medal]] "for his contributions to the theory of optimal transport, and its application to partial differential equations, metric geometry, and probability".<ref>[https://www.quantamagazine.org/alessio-figalli-a-mathematician-on-the-move-wins-fields-medal-20180801 A Traveler Who Finds Stability in the Natural World, August 1, 2018]</ref>

==Work==
Figalli has worked in the theory of [[Transportation theory (mathematics)|optimal transport]], with particular emphasis on the regularity theory of optimal transport maps and its connections to [[Monge–Ampère equation]]s. Amongst the results he obtained in this direction, there stand out an important higher integrability property of the second derivatives of solutions to the Monge–Ampère equation<ref>{{cite journal|title=<math>W^{2,1}</math> regularity for solutions of the Monge–Ampère equation |author= Guido De Philippis |author2=Alessio Figalli |doi=10.1007/s00222-012-0405-4 |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|arxiv=1111.7207|bibcode=2013InMat.192...55D|year= 2011 |volume= 192 |issue= 1 |pages= 55–69 |s2cid= 122492657 }}</ref> and a partial regularity result for Monge–Ampère type equations,<ref>{{cite journal |title=Partial regularity for optimal transport maps |author= Guido De Philippis |author2=Alessio Figalli |doi=10.1007/s10240-014-0064-7 |journal=Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS |volume= 121 |pages= 81–112 |arxiv=1209.5640 |year= 2015 |s2cid= 189795461 }}</ref> both proved together with [[Guido de Philippis]]. He used optimal transport techniques to get improved versions of the anisotropic [[isoperimetric inequality]], and obtained several other important results on the stability of functional and geometric inequalities. In particular, together with Francesco Maggi and Aldo Pratelli, he proved a sharp quantitative version of the anisotropic [[isoperimetric inequality]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=A mass transportation approach to quantitative isoperimetric inequalities |author= Alessio Figalli |author2=Francesco Maggi |author3=Aldo Pratelli |doi=10.1007/s00222-010-0261-z |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |volume= 182 |issue= 1 |pages= 167–211 |bibcode=2010InMat.182..167F |year= 2010 |s2cid= 10571756 }}</ref>

Then, in a joint work with [[Eric Anders Carlen|Eric Carlen]], he addressed the stability analysis of some [[Gagliardo–Nirenberg interpolation inequality|Gagliardo–Nirenberg]] and logarithmic [[Sobolev inequality|Hardy–Littlewood–Sobolev inequalities]] to obtain a quantitative rate of convergence for the critical mass Keller–Segel equation.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Stability for a GNS inequality and the Log-HLS inequality, with application to the critical mass Keller–Segel equation |author= Eric A. Carlen |author2=Alessio Figalli |doi=10.1215/00127094-2019931 |journal=Duke Mathematical Journal |volume= 162 |issue= 3 |pages= 579–625 |arxiv=1107.5976 |year= 2013 |s2cid= 14652858 }}</ref> He also worked on [[Hamilton–Jacobi equation]]s and their connections to weak [[Kolmogorov–Arnold–Moser theorem|Kolmogorov–Arnold–Moser theory]]. In a paper with Gonzalo Contreras and Ludovic Rifford, he proved generic hyperbolicity of Aubry sets on compact surfaces.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Generic hyperbolicity of Aubry sets on surfaces |author= Gonzalo Contreras |author2=Alessio Figalli |author3=Ludovic Rifford, L.|doi=10.1007/s00222-014-0533-0 |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume= 200 |issue= 1 |pages= 201–261 |bibcode=2015InMat.200..201C|year= 2015 |s2cid= 16312398 |url= https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-00935976 }}</ref>

In addition, he has given several contributions to the Di Perna–Lions' theory, applying it both to the understanding of [[Semiclassical physics|semiclassical]] limits of the [[Schrödinger equation]] with very rough potentials,<ref>{{cite journal |title=Semiclassical limit of quantum dynamics with rough potentials and well-posedness of transport equations with measure initial data |author= Luigi Ambrosio |author2=Alessio Figalli |author3=Gero Friesecke|display-authors=et al |doi=10.1002/cpa.20371 |journal=Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics |volume=64 |issue=9 |year=2011 |pages=1199–1242 |arxiv=1006.5388 |s2cid= 14331437 }}</ref> and to study the Lagrangian structure of weak solutions to the [[Vlasov equation|Vlasov–Poisson equation]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=On the Lagrangian structure of transport equations: The Vlasov–Poisson system |author= Luigi Ambrosio |author2=Maria Colombo |author2-link=Maria Colombo (mathematician)|author3=Alessio Figalli |doi=10.1215/00127094-2017-0032|journal=Duke Mathematical Journal |volume=166 |issue=18 |year=2017 |pages=3505–3568 |arxiv=1412.3608 |s2cid= 16821952 }}</ref> More recently, in collaboration with [[Alice Guionnet]], he introduced and developed new transportation techniques in the topic of [[random matrices]] to prove universality results in several-matrix models.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Universality in several-matrix models via approximate transport maps |author= Alessio Figalli |author2=Alice Guionnet |doi=10.1007/s11511-016-0142-4 |journal=Acta Mathematica |volume=217 |issue=1 |year=2016 |pages=81–176 |doi-access=free |arxiv=1407.2759 }}</ref> Also, together with Joaquim Serra, he proved the [[Ennio De Giorgi|De Giorgi]]'s conjecture for boundary reaction terms in dimension lower than five, and he improved the classical results by [[Luis Caffarelli]] on the structure of singular points in the [[obstacle problem]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=On the fine structure of the free boundary for the classical obstacle problem |author= Alessio Figalli |author2=Joaquim Serra |doi=10.1007/s00222-018-0827-8 |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |volume= 215 |pages= 311–366 |arxiv=1709.04002 |year= 2019 |issue= 1 |bibcode= 2019InMat.215..311F |s2cid= 119693672 }}</ref>
